Machine Intelligence

Unit 7 • SL

2 Weeks (6 Lessons) • A4.1.1, A4.1.1, A4.1.2, A4.4.1, A4.4.2

Unit Overview

of Computer Science Unit Foundation Concepts The core concept is the shift from Deterministic Programming (explicit instructions) to Probabilistic Learning (learning from data). Key themes include the Taxonomy of Learning (Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement, Transfer, and Deep Learning) and the Ethical Infrastructure required to manage autonomous decision-making.

What You'll Learn

  • A4.1.1 — Definitions of Artificial Intelligence (Narrow vs. General) and Machine Learning. Characteristics of Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement, Deep Learning, and Transfer Learning.
  • A4.1.1 — Applications: Medical imaging diagnostics, NLP, market basket analysis, robotics navigation, and sentiment analysis.
  • A4.1.2 — Hardware deployment: From standard laptops to advanced infrastructure (GPUs, TPUs, ASICs, FPGAs, Edge devices, and Cloud-based platforms).
  • A4.4.1 — Ethical implications: Accountability, algorithmic fairness, bias in training data, consent, and societal impact.
  • A4.4.2 — Emerging integration: Pervasive AI, Quantum computing, AR, and VR.

Key Terminology

Master these terms to succeed in this unit:

Narrow AI General AI Machine Learning Generative AI Supervised Unsupervised Reinforcement Deep Learning Transfer Learning GPU TPU ASIC Edge Device Algorithmic Fairness Bias Pervasive AI

Common Misconceptions

  • AI "Understanding": Students often believe AI has human-like intent or consciousness, rather than being a statistical engine finding generalizations in data.
  • General AI: Believing that "Strong AI" (human-level across all domains) is currently available technology (Textbook Clarification: only Narrow AI is available).
  • Data Objectivity: The belief that data is inherently neutral, ignoring that human bias is frequently encoded into training sets.

Big Ideas to Consider

  • Knowledge & Machines: Can a machine ever "know" something? Does knowledge reside outside human cognition?
  • Belief and Evidence: How does the rise of Generative AI and Deepfakes challenge the "seeing is believing" justification for knowledge?
